title: Protein sequence domain annotation using a language model
desc: Author summary Protein sequences are comprised of distinct functional units called domains. Identifying these domains is an important step in predicting protein function across large sequence databases. Most current domain annotation methods rely on scanning sequences against libraries of profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). Profile HMMs make several simplifying assumptions, which limit their ability to capture correlation between residues. We believe that domain annotation approaches could benefit from recent advances like protein language models that explicitly capture relationships between residues within and across domains. Here we present PSALM (protein sequence annotation using a language model), a domain annotation method that uses a protein language model and a probabilistic decoder to detect domains and define their boundaries in protein sequences. PSALM performs comparably to HMMER and shows improvements in detecting short, challenging domains. These results show that protein language models can encode evolutionary information that supports large-scale protein domain annotation.
